A young gunman who killed six people in central Krakow on ‌Saturday in Poland's unprecedented mass shooting has died in hospital, police said early ​on Monday.
Very little information ​has come out about the shooter, who was shot by ​police officers and arrested minutes ⁠after ⁠he opened fire ‌at people at Krakow's historic main square from his car.

The government said the assailant, a ⁠24-year-old from Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, a town of just under 60,000 in southeastern Poland, ‌may have been inspired by far-right ideology, without providing further details.

"There were many different emblems on ​the perpetrator’s clothing that have been partially ⁠examined and interpreted," Karolina Galecka, an ⁠interior ministry spokeswoman, told radio TOK FM ⁠on ⁠Monday.
"These ​patches were associated with various motifs ​that are currently ⁠being analyzed by specialists," she added, declining to comment further as the investigation is ongoing.
